answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost reduction with the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the assembly line at 94% capacity with no buffer. Historical evidence shows incumbent negotiation (memory_c4: margin recovery via benchmarking; memory_c6: multi-year commitments cut unit cost) can achieve cost reduction without delivery risk. Switching vendors (memory_c2) is too risky with no production buffer. Renewing unchanged (memory_c1) won't meet the cost mandate. Adding a second source (memory_c3) addresses supply risk but not the immediate cost target. Deferring (memory_c5) is infeasible with the 14-day deadline. Negotiating multi-year terms with the incumbent offers the best path to meet the cost target while preserving delivery stability.
